covered_number_domain: integers within ±9007199254740991 (every number a canonical determinism artifact holds)
out_of_scope: Fractional numbers, exponent forms and integers beyond the IEEE 754 safe range are not covered by these vectors: RFC 8785 defers those to ECMAScript Number::toString, and an approximate target would look authoritative and be wrong. Cover them in the TypeScript port against the official RFC 8785 conformance vectors.

rejected_inputs.name: lone_high_surrogate
rejected_inputs.rejection: Cannot read incomplete UTF-16 JSON text as string with missing low surrogate.
rejected_inputs.why: RFC 8785 §3.2.2 requires failing on invalid Unicode; a replacement character would canonicalize a string nobody supplied.

rejected_inputs.name: lone_low_surrogate
rejected_inputs.rejection: Cannot read invalid UTF-16 JSON text as string. Invalid surrogate value: '0xDE00'.
rejected_inputs.why: The same rule from the other half of the pair.

rejected_inputs.name: integer_beyond_safe_range
rejected_inputs.rejection: JCS reference serialization refuses the number '9007199254740993': only integers within ±9007199254740991 are covered (see this type's remarks). Extend the implementation deliberately rather than writing a target this code cannot compute correctly.
rejected_inputs.why: Outside the IEEE 754 safe range this reference implementation deliberately does not cover; see covered_number_domain.

vectors.name: object_key_ordering
vectors.note: Both rules sort object keys by UTF-16 code units and leave array order alone.

vectors.name: nested_structure
vectors.note: Nesting changes nothing: sorting is per object, array order is content.

vectors.name: scalars
vectors.note: Literals and small integers are written identically by both rules.

vectors.name: safe_integer_bounds
vectors.note: The widest integers a JSON reader can carry without losing bits.

vectors.name: artifact_shaped_fragment
vectors.note: A fragment shaped like the canonical determinism artifact the corpus actually carries.
